title: Human takeover stops the run immediately and no late dispatch escapes
risk: An agent keeps messaging a customer after a human operator takes over, so the customer receives conflicting answers from a bot and a person.
preconditions: Three-step plan for sess-a-1 in run orc-takeover-* where step 1 already completed
Operator takeover event delivered between step 1 and step 2 at 2026-01-15T10:05:00Z

steps.action: Deliver the takeover event and then let the worker attempt step 2
steps.expected: step 2 is never dispatched, the task reaches the stopped state and the takeover lock is present for the session

steps.action: Attempt a third dispatch through the messaging adapter with the same run
steps.expected: the dispatch is refused because the takeover check is re-evaluated before every step and retry

steps.action: Return the conversation to the agent with a resume event
steps.expected: the takeover lock is released, the conversation returns to auto routing and the stopped run stays terminal

steps.action: Send a new inbound signal for the session
steps.expected: a fresh run starts with its own run id and does not resume the stopped run

assertions: Exactly one step (step 1) was dispatched before the takeover; steps 2 and 3 produced zero dispatches
The takeover lock exists while the operator holds the session and is gone after the resume event
The post-takeover signal produces a new run id distinct from the stopped one
forbidden: Dispatch any message while the takeover lock is held
Resurrect the stopped run after the operator returns the conversation to the agent
evidence: Per-step dispatch log for the run with the takeover timestamp marked
Takeover lock presence before and after resume plus the new run id record
cleanup: Release the takeover lock and delete the run-scoped rows for orc-takeover-*; keep audit entries
automation: Drive the real session-control and step engine with a recording messaging adapter; the oracle is the per-step dispatch log around the takeover timestamp, not a lock-configuration read.
